lines.text: Napoleon versus three thousand rabbits. This actually happened. Probably.
lines.note: Based on the memoirs of General Paul Thiébault

lines.text: 1807. Napoleon has just signed a peace treaty, so his chief of staff throws him a celebration rabbit hunt.
lines.note: July 1807 · after the Treaties of Tilsit · hosted by Marshal Berthier

lines.text: Quick fact: Napoleon wasn't short. About five foot seven. Average for his time.
lines.note: About 1.69 m · the myth: French inches + British cartoons

lines.text: The cages open. But these rabbits were bought from local farmers. They're tame.
lines.note: Accounts range from hundreds to 3,000 rabbits

lines.text: So instead of running away, they think it's dinner time. And they charge.
The greatest general in Europe tries to fight them off with his riding crop.
It doesn't work. He retreats to his carriage, and the rabbits split up and flank him.
Some of them reportedly got inside the carriage.
Winner? The rabbits. According to one general's memoir. A general who hated the host.
lines.note: Thiébault's memoirs (1894) · he had a long feud with Berthier
